summary: Partition a UTF-8 string into custom-graphemes via 6 boundary rules, output grapheme indices as UTF-16 offsets, and find longest common suffix match.

traps.quote: output the UTF-16 offsets of boundaries i,j... A scalar at most U+FFFF occupies one UTF-16 code unit; a larger scalar occupies two.
traps.consequence: Outputs byte offsets or UTF-8 positions instead of UTF-16 code-unit offsets, causing wrong answers for strings with emoji.
traps.guard: Track each grapheme boundary's UTF-8 byte position; decode scalars to count 1 or 2 UTF-16 units per scalar.

traps.quote: For each internal gap between adjacent Unicode scalar values, apply the first matching rule... rule order is authoritative.
traps.consequence: Merges rule conditions or checks all rules instead of stopping at first match, causing false boundaries or missing boundaries.
traps.guard: Implement if-else-if chain: check rules 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in order; stop on first true condition; use rule 6 as catch-all.

traps.quote: If the left scalar is U+200D, the right scalar is an Emoji, and the nearest scalar before that U+200D after skipping Attachments is an Emoji, there is no boundary.
traps.consequence: Fails to skip Attachments when looking backward from U+200D, or misidentifies Emoji ranges, causing wrong boundaries.
traps.guard: When left is U+200D and right is Emoji: walk backward from U+200D skipping Attachment ranges, check final scalar is Emoji.

traps.quote: If both scalars are Regional Indicators, count the consecutive Regional Indicators ending at the left scalar. There is no boundary exactly when that count is odd.
traps.consequence: Miscounts consecutive RI by starting from wrong position or not including left scalar, giving wrong parity check.
traps.guard: Count RI by walking backward from left scalar (inclusive) until hitting non-RI; apply no-boundary iff count is odd.

traps.quote: resolve an index x to x when nonnegative and G+x when negative, then clamp it to [0,G]
traps.consequence: Clamps before resolving, or clamps to [1,G], causing invalid grapheme indices and wrong query results.
traps.guard: First compute resolved = (x if x >= 0 else G+x); then clamp(resolved, 0, G); apply this to both query indices.

traps.quote: for every 0<=k<L, grapheme i+k and grapheme j+k have identical UTF-8 byte sequences... 600,000 bytes and 300,000 queries
traps.consequence: Naive byte-by-byte comparison per query gives O(Q*L*bytes) ≈ O(10^11), timing out.
traps.guard: Precompute grapheme boundaries and byte ranges; for each query, iterate in O(L) comparing byte ranges; handle early exit.

input_shape: UTF-8 string S (no ASCII whitespace, ≤600KB), then Q (≤300K) queries with signed i64 indices.
output_shape: Two decimal integers per query: UTF-16 offsets or match length and byte count.
invariants: Grapheme boundaries indexed [0,G]; negative indices resolve to G+x before clamping.
Rules 1-6 applied in order; first match stops evaluation, no merging of conditions.
UTF-16 offset = count of code units: U+0000..U+FFFF = 1 unit, U+10000+ = 2 units.
max_scale: 600,000 UTF-8 bytes, 300,000 queries, grapheme count up to ~600,000.
